newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azerbaijan says prevented coup, dozens arrested.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan says prevented coup, dozens arrested.

text.p: More than 40 people have been arrested in Azerbaijan and accused of plotting to assassinate President Haidar Aliyev and stage a coup, officials said on Tuesday.

A joint statement by the National Security Ministry, the prosecutor's office and the Interior Ministry said those arrested had been involved in plans by former president Ayaz Mutalibov and his allies to overthrow Aliyev.
It said the coup had been planned to take place late last year in the Transcaucasus state.
Azerbaijan, on the volatile southern rim of the former Soviet Union, has vast oil reserves and has attracted tens of billions of dollars in foreign energy investments.
Aliyev keeps a close watch his political opponents and there have been many crackdowns on the opposition.
Human rights activists said they were alarmed by the detentions.

"Knowing how arrested people have been treated in the past, the announcement of new arrests is alarming. The overall picture of human rights in Azerbaijan is very grim," said Moscow-based Rachel Denber of Human Rights Watch/Helsinki.

The statement said the plot would have been the fourth attempt to seize power in Azerbaijan since October 1994. About 2,000 people had been arrested over that period on charges of terrorist activities and plotting to seize power, it said.
Denber quoted local rights activists as saying more than 1,000 people were now in prison over alleged participation in coup attempts or on treason charges.
"Many of those arrested on political grounds suffered torture and many were tortured to death," she said.
Mutalibov was ousted in 1992. Aliyev, the former Soviet republic's Communist Party boss, came to power in 1993 after another former leader was ousted in a military coup.
Five people were arrested in June last year and charged with involvement in an alleged plot to kill Aliyev in 1993.
Many former government officials have been sentenced to death, but there has rarely been confirmation of the sentences being carried out.
